title: LightML: A Photonic Accelerator for Efficient General Purpose Machine Learning
problem: General-purpose machine learning workloads require massive computational throughput that strains conventional electronic server infrastructure in terms of cost and power. Existing photonic computing proposals lack a complete system-level design with proper memory and buffer support to fully utilize the high-speed photonic crossbar.
motivation: Photonic crossbars can perform matrix-vector multiplications at the speed of light with near-zero switching energy, but realizing their throughput advantage requires solving the memory interface and functional-unit gap that prior photonic ML accelerators left unaddressed.
method: LightML implements the first complete system-level photonic crossbar design for ML, pairing a photonic crossbar core with a carefully co-designed memory and buffer architecture that sustains greater than 80% utilization of the photonic crossbar. The system supports large-scale matrix-matrix multiplication (MMM), element-wise operations, non-linear activation functions, and convolutional layers via dedicated photonic and electronic functional units. The design targets both edge and data-center density profiles, delivering 325 TOP/s at 3 W.
key_novelty: First system-level photonic crossbar design that includes a purpose-built memory and buffer architecture enabling sustained high utilization (>80%) of the photonic core across diverse ML operations.
contributions: First complete system-level photonic crossbar architecture optimized for ML with >80% crossbar utilization
Memory and buffer architecture co-designed to match the high-speed photonic crossbar throughput
Hardware support for large-scale MMM, element-wise ops, non-linear functions, and convolutional layers
Demonstrated 325 TOP/s at 3 W, suitable for edge and dense data-center deployments
limitations: Baselines and direct comparison to electronic or prior photonic accelerators not discussed in the abstract.
